newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul stocks close higher despite profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Seoul stocks close higher despite profit-taking.

text.p: The Seoul stock market finished slightly higher on Tuesday backed by gains in heavily-weighted POSCO and KEPCO, but late profit-taking cancelled out many of the early sharp rises, brokers said.
The composite index rose 2.29 points to 797.62, off an intraday high of 806.12. Losers slightly beat gainers by 453 to 409 with 100 stocks going limit up.
"Rises in POSCO and KEPCO contributed to today's gain," said Kim Duck-sun, broker at Hyundai Securities.
But profit-taking in reaction to steep rises since Monday emerged, paring most of the early sharp gains.
Steelmaker POSCO and electricity-monopoly KEPCO added 900 won and 1,000 won each to 43,700 and 26,500 respectively.
"The market proved it would be difficult to lift shares across the board, given the current level of market energy," said Park Sang-jae, analyst at Coryo Securities.

Some brokers said the market was supported by expectations that the government would unveil some measures to stimulate the economy and boost competitiveness on Wednesday at an economic ministers' meeting.
Many believe the government will cut the reserve requirement for banks, a move seen prodding commercial banks to trim rates.
But Park said the ratio cut could be dropped from the government's agenda. "If not, there are no reasons for cheap large-caps and banks not to sustain their strength," he said.
Officials declined to comment on the speculation.

Shares in Daewoo Group failed to repeat Monday's hefty gains. Daewoo Heavy Industries rose 140 won to 7,100 with the largest trading volume of 1.16 million shares. But Daewoo Corp and Daewoo Electronics lost 30 won and 100 won each to 7,600 and 6,740 respectively.
But investors renewed their strong but selective interest in individual small-cap shares. -- YEOM YOON-JEONG (822) 727 5647
